subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should OpenClaw accept dashboard widget write-back as a bundled dashboard capability, and should its persisted widget state use the plugin-state SQLite store instead of per-widget JSON files?
rationale: This changes the sandboxed widget trust boundary and persistent state model, and the repository policy already constrains both plugin boundaries and runtime storage choices.

options.title: Adopt after Wave 1 with SQLite state
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement it only after the base dashboard stack lands, using plugin-scoped SQLite state plus explicit capability, approval, size, rebroadcast, and adversarial tests.

options.title: Defer to roadmap only
options.body: Leave the roadmap item open but do not start implementation until maintainers settle the broader modular dashboard direction and security review.

options.title: Reject widget write-back for now
options.body: Close the direction as too much trust-surface expansion unless a narrower stateful-widget need and security model is approved later.

recommendation.title: Adopt after Wave 1 with SQLite state
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement it only after the base dashboard stack lands, using plugin-scoped SQLite state plus explicit capability, approval, size, rebroadcast, and adversarial tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current bundled Control UI plugin-tab seam and its merge history route this product/security choice through the same area owner.
